title: Microsoft Purview, Azure Policy and resource locks
learningObjective: Describe the purpose of Microsoft Purview, Azure Policy and resource locks, and how they work together with RBAC.
foundation: Microsoft Purview is a family of data governance, risk and compliance tools: it helps you find, classify and protect your data wherever it is (Azure, on-premises, Microsoft 365, other clouds).
Azure Policy enforces rules on your Azure resources, such as 'only these regions' or 'storage must use HTTPS'. It can block non-compliant deployments, flag them, or fix them.
Resource locks stop accidental deletion or change. CanNotDelete (shown as Delete) allows changes but not deletion; ReadOnly allows neither. Locks apply to everyone, even Owners.
engineer: Microsoft Purview: two main areas: risk and compliance (Microsoft 365 data: protect sensitive data in Teams, OneDrive, Exchange; manage data lifecycle; insider risk; compliance requirements) and unified data governance (data map that discovers and classifies data across sources such as Azure SQL, Azure Data Lake, on-premises SQL Server, Amazon S3, Power BI; data catalog; data lineage).

Azure Policy: definitions (rules in JSON), initiatives (groups of policies, for example a regulatory standard), and assignments at a scope (management group, subscription, resource group, resource), inherited downward. Effects include Deny, Audit, Append, Modify, DeployIfNotExists and AuditIfNotExists.

Policy evaluates resources when they're created or updated and periodically; the Compliance view lists non-compliant resources. Remediation tasks fix existing resources for Modify/DeployIfNotExists policies. Hundreds of built-in definitions exist; Defender for Cloud and regulatory compliance build on Policy.

Resource locks: applied at subscription, resource group or resource; inherited by child resources. Order of checks: a request passes RBAC (are you allowed?), then Azure Policy (is it compliant?), then locks (is it locked?). To delete a locked resource, an Owner or User Access Administrator must remove the lock first.
ReadOnly can have side effects: for example on a storage account it blocks listing keys, and on a VM it blocks start/restart because those are POST operations.

example.title: Keeping production safe
body: A retailer assigns 'Allowed locations' (Deny) and 'Require a tag' at its production management group. Developers who try to create resources in another region are blocked even with Contributor.
The production database has a CanNotDelete lock, so even an Owner must remove it before deleting. Microsoft Purview scans the database and labels columns containing card numbers as sensitive.

prerequisites: An Azure subscription (a free account works)
permissions: Resource Policy Contributor to assign policies; Owner or User Access Administrator to create or delete locks
portal: Policy > Assignments > Assign policy; Policy > Compliance.
Resource / resource group > Settings > Locks > Add.
Microsoft Purview portal (purview.microsoft.com): Data Map, sources, scans.
configuration.cli:
az policy assignment create --name allowed-locations --policy e56962a6-4747-49cd-b67b-bf8b01975c4c --params "{\"listOfAllowedLocations\":{\"value\":[\"westeurope\",\"northeurope\"]}}" --scope /subscriptions/<sub>
az lock create --name keep --lock-type CanNotDelete -g rg-prod

troubleshooting.cause: A Deny policy blocks the configuration.
troubleshooting.fix: Change the deployment to comply, or request an exemption.

troubleshooting.symptom: Can't restart a VM in a resource group.
troubleshooting.cause: A ReadOnly lock blocks POST operations.
troubleshooting.fix: Use CanNotDelete instead, or remove the lock temporarily.

comparisons.difference: RBAC controls what users can do; Policy controls what resources can look like, for everyone.
CanNotDelete allows changes; ReadOnly blocks changes too.

misconceptions.reality: The lock must be removed first.
Deny blocks, Modify and DeployIfNotExists change resources.

misconceptions.myth: Purview is only for Azure data.
misconceptions.reality: It covers on-premises, Microsoft 365 and other clouds.

architectureDecisions: Lock critical production resources with CanNotDelete.
Use Purview to discover and classify sensitive data.
